title: A jar object
scenario: Two jars, A and B. Add n cookies to A only, then print both counts.

intro.job: Two jars, A and B. Add n cookies to A only, then print both counts.

idea.rule: Class attributes are the shared whiteboard; self. attributes are each jar's own label — write on the wrong one and everyone sees it.
idea.detail: Anything set directly in the class body (count = 0) belongs to the class — every jar reads the same one. self.count = 0 inside __init__ runs once per new jar and gives THAT jar its own count. Inside a method, self.count means 'this jar's count'; Jar.count means 'the shared one'.

        self.count = 0
    def add(self, n):
        self.count += n

why_line: count lives on the class and add changes Jar.count — there's only one count, shared by every jar, so B reads the 3 too.

explain.rule: Jar.count is the whiteboard in the kitchen: write 3 on it for jar A, and jar B — reading the same board — says 3 as well.
explain.bridge: So where should each jar keep its own count?

fix.rule: self.count = 0 in __init__ gives each new jar its own label; self.count += n writes only on this jar's label.

walk.gloss: Make jar A — __init__ gives it its own count of 0.
Make jar B — its own count of 0 too.
Add n to A's count only.
